acceptance: Under pytest, no test can read the real `~/.benchbox` credentials. A test proves this by seeding a sentinel credential in a fake real-home location and asserting it never appears in a built config.
Any API that returns a config containing secrets returns them masked in its repr, str and log output. A test covers this.
The guard also covers isolation with marker selection, such as `-m` live-only expressions, the case #2970 handled for logging.
Under pytest, no test writes to the real `~/.benchbox` (for example `last_run.yaml`); a test seeds a sentinel file there and asserts it is unchanged after a CLI run
context: Merged as PR 3273. Finding: HOME isolation under pytest already worked (session_isolation replaces HOME and USERPROFILE before conftest, and is dropped only for live_integration-only selections); the gap was the missing proof and that a built DatabaseConfig printed secrets. Done: (1) tests/unit/test_session_isolation.py seeds a sentinel credentials.yaml and a last_run.yaml in the caller's home and runs a real pytest subprocess: an isolated run never sees the sentinel in a built snowflake config and leaves the home byte-for-byte unchanged; the same probe under -m live_integration (which keeps the caller's home on purpose) does see the sentinel and does write there, so neither check passes trivially. (2) DatabaseConfig now redacts secret-named options and fields and URI-embedded credentials in repr, str, format and log output, using is_secret_option_key and sanitize_platform_options; model_dump and attribute access still return real values; an unset secret renders as None. With the fix reverted 7 of 9 masking tests fail, and the output shows the registry-built config printing the password. (3) Live-only marker selection was already pinned by existing tests. Not changed on purpose: CredentialManager.get_platform_credentials returns the live internal dict that callers mutate and save_credentials serialises with yaml.dump, so a masking dict subclass there would risk writing Python object tags into credentials.yaml; get_display_credentials already masks for display. Unconfirmed: the 2026-10-16 observation that last_run.yaml changed during a -n 8 run. The isolated probe leaves the home untouched, so the likely cause is a run whose -m selection kept the caller's home, or a process outside pytest; no test path writing to the real home was found.
description: A worker called `PlatformHookRegistry.build_database_config("snowflake", ...)` in a local probe. The returned config contained the real Snowflake credential set from `~/.benchbox`, and the worker printed it to its terminal. Nothing reached the repository or a PR. The takeover handoff also says that this API loads real saved credentials into the returned config during tests. Tests and probes that build a config can therefore read, and may log or write, real user secrets.
